text:
incident-bot: ALERT: GPU-POOL-south-east queue depth exceeded 1200 requests (threshold 800) · autoscaler failed 3x to add nodes · affected pools: gpu-prod-1,gpu-prod-2

Maya Patel: paging oncall — I'm seeing high queue depth on prod inference. multiple timeouts from frontend.

Nadia Rivera: oncall ack. pulling logs now. ETA 2m.

Arun Gupta: I'm seeing repeated autoscaler errors: `Failed to allocate instance: quota_exceeded` in the cloud logs. Also a bunch of nodes reporting CUDA Xid 33 followed by driver restarts.

Liza Chen: Xid 33 = GPU page fault / memory issue — that will drop the node out of the pool. Are we seeing OOMs in container logs too?

Maya Patel: yes Liza, container OOMs for a few customer-heavy workloads. Mixed with many short-running requests so batching is not aggregating. Throttle kicking in.

incident-bot: PagerDuty incident created: PD-3482 · Sev 1 · Assigned to oncall: Nadia Rivera

Nadia Rivera: quick impact check — which customers on Dedicated? Sam, can you correlate customer SLAs?

Sam Ortiz: looking. Two paying customers on Dedicated have 20-30% increased latency and error rates (500s) in the last 10m. No total outage yet, but degraded for heavy-retry endpoints.

Arun Gupta: autoscaler logs show `scale_up_attempt(3): rejected by quota manager` and `scale_up_backoff` — we hit region-level GPU quota. Requests queued are growing because driver instability has reduced effective capacity by ~25% across the pool.

Liza Chen: stacktrace from runtime on one node: 
```
2026-03-15T21:04:12Z runtime ERROR: allocation failed: cudaErrorLaunchOutOfResources (2)
... kernel aborted, Xid 33
```
Also `nvlink` health shows intermittent flapping on GPUS-2 on the node.

Maya Patel: immediate mitigation proposals: 1) drain the worst nodes, 2) temporarily increase fallback capacity by routing a small % to smaller-quantized model variant, 3) request emergency quota bump with cloud ops. Thoughts?

Arun Gupta: concur. I'll open a quota request right now and simultaneously spin up fallback instances in another region if we can cross-region route. Spinning up normally blocked by quota but we have some spare in west-eu that we can use — need network acceptance.

Liza Chen: draining nodes: recommend `kubectl cordon` + `kubectl drain` with `--ignore-daemonsets` on nodes hitting Xid repeatedly. But we should mark them unschedulable in the pool to avoid re-adding. I'll prepare the node list.

Maya Patel: do it. Also enable model-level backoff: 10% of chat/generation traffic -> `small-quant` variant. That reduces per-request GPU memory and latency. Patch route via runtime quick flag: `--route-fallback=small-quant:10%`.

Arun Gupta: opened cloud support ticket 110223, requested emergency +50 GPUs in region; ETA support response 15-30m. Also I started cross-region spin-up: `launch-template fallbacks-west-eu --count 40 --tag emergency` (will show as pending until quota confirmed).

Liza Chen: drained nodes list (nodes with >3 Xid in 10m): node-gpu-09,node-gpu-11,node-gpu-14. Executing drains now. Command: 
```
for n in 09 11 14; do kubectl cordon node-gpu-$n && kubectl drain node-gpu-$n --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data; done
```

Maya Patel: nice. After drain, update routing to avoid pool gpu-prod-1. I pushed a runtime patch to temporarily exclude that pool from allocation. `runtimectl pool disable gpu-prod-1`.

incident-bot: NOTE: pool gpu-prod-1 marked DISABLED by Maya Patel at 21:08:03Z

Sam Ortiz: customer comms draft: "We're experiencing degraded inference performance in US-South region due to driver/runtime instability; we're routing traffic to fallback capacity and working with cloud provider to add capacity. We'll follow up with timeline once we stabilize." Approve and send?

Nadia Rivera: send. Add link to status page and mention some requests may see higher latency.

Maya Patel: sending now. Also enabling temporary token-based rate-limiting to prevent noisy noisy tenants from hammering. `ratelimitctl set tenant noisy-tenant-xyz 50r/s`.

Arun Gupta: cloud support just replied: they can add quota if we provide justification and plan to rebalance load off the impacted pool. They approved a soft reserve of +32 GPUs while we wait for formal approval. I'm launching them now in a spare subnetwork.

Liza Chen: runtime health after drains: KV cache hit ratio dropped slightly, but overall active GPU memory per-node improved. Error count for Xid on drained nodes stopped (obvious), remaining nodes still show low intermittent GPU ECC messages but stable.

Maya Patel: monitoring: queue depth down from 1.3k to 600 in last 8m. Error rate 500s down from 7% to 2.1%. Latency p95 improved by 300ms for affected endpoints.

Sam Ortiz: customers acknowledged comms, two asked for incident bridge — they asked to be present for postmortem. I've scheduled a 30m sync tomorrow with the two customers and engineering to review root cause and mitigation plan.

Nadia Rivera: handoff: I need to go for a quick break in 6m. Maya, can you take the next 30m on-call actions? I'll stay reachable for escalations.

Maya Patel: taking handoff. Will monitor autoscaler and cloud quota progress.

Arun Gupta: follow-up: opening an infra ticket to investigate driver kernel build on nodes that flapped — suspect an older NVIDIA driver + specific CUDA kernel regression. Ticket INFRA-792

Liza Chen: runtime TODOs: add Xid surge detector to runtime metrics so we can auto-evacuate nodes earlier; add golden prompt set to detect quantized-model quality regressions when we auto-fallback; add clearer fallback percent knob in console.

incident-bot: PD-3482 status changed to "under control" by Maya Patel at 21:18:53Z · notes: queue reduced, fallback active, quota request pending

Maya Patel: quick summary for postmortem: root cause = driver/runtime instability (Xid/OOM) reduced effective capacity; autoscaler couldn't recover due to region GPU quota limits causing queue growth and throttling; immediate mitigations = drain flapping nodes, enable fallback model routing, emergency quota request, cross-region fallback spin-up, temporary rate-limits; impact = degraded latency and 500s for some customers (no total outage).

Nadia Rivera: agreed. Will create incident doc in #postmortems with timeline and attach logs. Assigning owners: infra (Arun) driver investigation, runtime (Liza) metrics + fallback improvements, GtM (Sam) customer comms follow-up.

Sam Ortiz: will coordinate customer follow-up and put recs in the customer-facing summary.

Maya Patel: closing notes: keep an eye on ECC/gpu-health and autoscale quota alarms for next 24h. Re-enable pool gpu-prod-1 only after driver patch + 1h of stability testing.

incident-bot: Incident PD-3482 updated · severity lowered to SEV-2 pending review · follow-up meeting scheduled 2026-03-16T10:00Z

Nadia Rivera: leaving handoff to Maya. thanks team, good rapid moves. :thumbsup:

Maya Patel: thanks all — will update thread when we re-enable pool or get quota confirmed.

Arun Gupta: quota confirmed by cloud at 21:32Z, additional GPUs are active and routing is rebalanced. I'll keep the infra ticket updated.

Liza Chen: runtime note: I pushed a temporary hotfix to avoid local kernel prefetch on the affected nodes (reduces memory pressure). We'll validate and roll to AM release if stable.

Maya Patel: thread will remain for postmortem notes. marking incident as mitigated for now.

incident-bot: Incident PD-3482 mitigated at 21:36:12Z by Maya Patel
